So I'm adding some elements of Spelljammer to my campaign and I was wondering if you guys had any tips or tricks from someone who has done it before? I've only know about Spelljammer for about two months and never actually played AD&D module but I could see some fun interactions with some of the Pathfinder creatures from the Distant Worlds book.
Add Spelljammer to an existing campaign, any ideas?

I like to keep it subtle. Some strange creatures in the marketplace or a ship appearing in the water where there was no ship before. Make it a mystery and a background thing as you slow play your way towards D&D IN SPAAAAAAACE!

See I've been running this campaign story line since August of last year and the entire time there was this extra-planar enemy behind the scenes that the players are aware of. This enemy kept visiting their plane and setting up cults or stealing stuff and the players have only slowly gotten hints about what was happening. It finally came to a head when they killed the Big Bad Evil guys right hand man and discovered a broken Spelljammer as well as a journal from an Arcane who had crashed to Golarian hundreds of years earlier. So the players now know that the Evil Dude has been using a Spelljammer to get to where they are, and that this mage's plan is to trap a god in a mortal body and bring that god to their own plane where there are no gods, So now the players just need to stop it, and when they do, it will be the end of the year long adventure and the new one will begin with them having a Spelljammer and being the first explorers from Golarian to leave the planet.

Decide ahead of time if you want to actually use the mechanics or just hand wave it as "speed of plot" kind of stuff. There ARE rules for how much air a ship can maintain, how fast it can go etc. but I think you can run it just fine by hand-waving that stuff away. They have as much air as they need, it takes them as long as it takes to get where they're going, enemy ships are either faster or slower etc.
